title: Continuously verify security and compliance
objective: Evaluate access, configuration, detection, and audit evidence separately, and safely remediate deviations.

sections.title: Apply least privilege to each principal
paragraphs: Security administrators do not treat people, applications, and execution roles for automation as the same principal. IAM policies limit who can perform which actions on which resources under which conditions, and temporary credentials are preferred over long-term credentials.

When investigating a permissions issue, verify effective permissions by considering not only identity-based policies, but also resource-based policies, permissions boundaries, organizational controls, and explicit denies. Granting administrator permissions is not a substitute for investigation.

sections.title: Turning Configuration History and Relationships into Evidence
paragraphs: AWS Config provides information that lets you review the configuration details of AWS resources, the relationships between resources, and configuration history. Security personnel can track not only the current configuration, but also when changes occurred, which principal made them, and which related resources were changed.

A compliance assessment maps requirements, target resources, evaluation rules, exception approvals, and remediation results to one another. Rather than simply closing findings, it verifies that the configuration complies after remediation and that the same deviation does not recur.

sections.title: Responding to Detection Findings by Priority
paragraphs: Security operators do not automatically remediate every finding from detection services in the same way. They assess the affected accounts, resources, data, exposure paths, and confidence in the detection, then carry out responses such as isolation, credential invalidation, and evidence preservation according to priority.

After an incident, preserve CloudTrail records, configuration history, network logs, and other evidence so that what happened can be traced. Do not delete evidence or disable notifications before confirming the cause.

checkpoints.prompt: An access denial has occurred for an IAM role used for operational automation. Select one scope of effective permissions that an administrator should examine to investigate the cause.

choices.text: Permanently add administrator permissions to the role without determining the cause.
choices.explanation: This undermines least privilege and may not resolve the cause of the denial.

choices.text: Run the automation using shared, long-term access keys.
choices.explanation: This weakens the identification of the principal and the management of credentials.

choices.text: Review the effective permissions, including identity-based policies, resource-based policies, permissions boundaries, organizational controls, and explicit denies.
choices.explanation: Permissions are determined by multiple controls, and explicit denies take precedence.

checkpoints.prompt: A security officer is investigating when a prohibited-public-access S3 bucket configuration was changed. Select one combination of evidence that is most appropriate.

choices.text: Check only the current bucket name.
choices.explanation: This does not reveal the time of the change or who made it.

choices.text: Correlate the AWS Config configuration history and resource relationships with the CloudTrail operation history by time and target resource.
choices.explanation: This allows the configuration change to be linked to the operation that performed it.

choices.text: Delete the logs before starting the investigation.
choices.explanation: This would result in the loss of necessary evidence.

checkpoints.prompt: A detection service has notified you of suspicious use of credentials. Select the single most appropriate action for the security operator to take first.

choices.text: Disable the notification and keep no records.
choices.explanation: This could cause ongoing compromise to go undetected.
This would halt business operations without assessing the impact.

choices.text: Confirm the affected principals, resources, exposure paths, and detection confidence; then, as necessary, isolate the affected components, disable the credentials, and preserve the evidence.
choices.explanation: This limits the impact while preserving the information needed for subsequent investigation.
